To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
credit constraints have a significant impact on international trade.

financial development increases a country's exports above and beyond the effect on aggregate production, that the increase in exports is due to an increase in the number of exporting firms and a reduction in the export intensity of firms that export, that the effect is larger in financially vulnerable sectors, and that the effect is due to a reduction in firm level exports and an increase in the variety of products exported.

financial development increases exports, increases the range of products traded, reduces turnover in product lines, increases the number of destinations exported to, and increases export to smaller destinations.
In summary, our research is concerned with
understanding the mechanisms by which credit constraints affect trade and the implications of this effect for economic growth.
the impact of financial market imperfection on international trade.
how the financial system influences the behavior of the firm and how the behavior of the firms in turn influences economic activity.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
credit market imperfections have a strong impact on trade, and this impact is not only on the aggregate but also on the microeconomic level.
the results of this study show that financial market imperfections have a strong impact on the pattern of trade and the composition of exports of developing countries.
credit constraints reduce trade in two ways, first through the reduction of firm level exports and second through the reduction of product variety and the increase in turnover.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
financial market imperfections can be a significant source of comparative advantage.
credit constraints are detrimental for international trade.
financial development is a necessary condition for the success of trade liberalization.
The main takeaway from our work is that
credit constraints have an important impact on the composition of trade and that this impact is heterogeneous across countries and sectors.
the financial system plays a critical role in determining a country's trade performance.
financial development can help countries overcome credit constraints and improve their trade performance.
